_notes: Frontmatter `allowed-tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Task` and `license: LICENSE` are NOT representable in descriptor v0. See descriptor-schema-v0.md §'Known v0 gaps'. Flagged in phase0-2-report.md.
The 'research vs reporting' distinction in the spec is embedded in prompt text — the descriptor can only express this via prompt content, not as a separate scope artefact.

inputs.name: code
inputs.description: Code or diff to review for security vulnerabilities.

description.template:
Verify exploitability for vulnerability `{candidate.vuln_id}` ({candidate.category}) at `{candidate.location}`.

Research the data flow: where does the input come from? Is it attacker-controlled (request.GET, request.POST, request.json, request.headers, request.cookies, URL path segments, file uploads, WebSocket messages) — or server-controlled (settings.*, os.environ, config files, hardcoded constants, signed session data)?

Does the framework mitigate this? (Django auto-escape, React JSX escape, ORM parameterization, etc.) Is there upstream validation or sanitization?

Return confidence HIGH only when you have a vulnerable pattern AND attacker-controlled input AND no framework mitigation. Return MEDIUM when the input source is unclear. Return LOW for theoretical / defense-in-depth issues.

Candidate snippet:
{candidate.snippet}

Reviewer rationale: {candidate.rationale}

description.value: If confidence is HIGH, severity, issue_description and fix MUST be populated. If confidence is MEDIUM or LOW, these MAY be null.

description.template: Build the final SecurityReviewReport. Include only HIGH-confidence verdicts in `findings`. Put MEDIUM-confidence verdicts in `needs_verification`. Drop LOW-confidence verdicts entirely. Compute risk_level from the highest severity in findings. If no high-confidence vulnerabilities exist, summary = 'No high-confidence vulnerabilities identified.'

description.value: Findings list must contain only items with HIGH confidence. Do not invent issues that weren't in the verification step.
